extracted.intended_audience: Members and chairs of ALSC award committees (e.g., Randolph Caldecott Medal Committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for serving on an ALSC award committee: eligibility, relationships with publishers, meeting procedures, identifying/reading/notes, nomination/balloting processes, and selection of winners and honor books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting attendance and access to materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons elected or appointed to an award committee should: 1) Be able to attend all required discussion and decision meetings, in person and virtual, scheduled for the year of service ... and be able to follow procedures established by the committee. 2) Have ready access to the major part of the current output of children’s books under consideration in outlets such as their local library or bookstore and through interlibrary loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required meetings include pre-scheduled virtual meetings in July after Annual conference, virtual meetings in two weeks prior to LibLearnX, and the in-person LibLearnX final selection meeting. If a committee member cannot obtain an occasional title, arrangements for review copies may be made per committee guidelines (see Relationship with Publishers). Although these requirements may limit membership, complete participation of all members is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of service restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may serve on the Batchelder Award, Caldecott Medal, Geisel Award, Newbery Medal, Sibert Medal, Children’s Literature Legacy Award, or Notable Children’s Books Committee more often than once every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four-year period begins from the last year of the term of service regardless of term length. Rule does not apply to appointment as Chair or to other ALSC committees. May be suspended for emergency mid-year replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with publishers — accepting unsolicited books
rubrics_metrics.description: Many publishers send committee members eligible books for consideration. Committee members may accept these unsolicited books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair compiles publisher mailing roster; ALSC Awards Coordinator shares roster with publishers. Chair surveys members to track missing titles; Chair/PGC may contact publishers for difficult-to-obtain titles. Members should not solicit publishers for free, personal copies—members accept appointment with understanding they have access to new books and are responsible for obtaining them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with publishers — avoiding conflicts and favors
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are cautioned to avoid any conflicts of interest that might grow out of personal contact with personnel involved in publishing children’s books. Committee members are not to solicit publishers for favors, invitations, or the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to suspend contacts so long as there's express understanding such contacts do not influence consideration or choices. Unsolicited offers may be accepted only with the express understanding they do not influence book consideration or final choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher submission procedures and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit works for consideration ... publishers should: Review the terms and criteria for the award. Submit one copy of the work to the award committee Chair. The deadline for submitting books for consideration is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers may optionally send a copy to each committee member but it is not required. A list of committee members is available via award Terms and Criteria page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of self-published and small-press titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Books that are self-published or published by small presses are eligible, provided they meet all other eligibility requirements. Books are eligible in their first year of publication only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If self-published book is later commercially republished by another publisher, it will not be reconsidered. Chair keeps/pass on a current year’s list of award-eligible books received directly from authors or small presses; sharing with committee is at the Chair’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair responsibilities — welcome and calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair should send a letter of welcome including an outline of the year’s work and upcoming issues, distribute the calendar of the year’s work and meetings as soon as possible, and establish/distribute meeting agendas and logistical arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Welcome should encourage members to focus on the committee manual and Reading Lists. Chair must set calendar early (see Appendix C sample calendar) and alert members to mandatory virtual meetings and LibLearnX timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee communication protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair will establish ground rules for all forms of communication at the beginning of term. A video conferencing platform will be used for virtual meetings. Electronic communication will be used to distribute information and discuss procedural issues. Substantial book discussions among committee members will be limited to in-person or virtual committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email is not used for substantive discussion and is not a substitute for face-to-face/virtual discussions; email may be used for eligibility or factual-error questions, which the Chair decides whether to bring to full committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting attendance responsibility and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are responsible for attending all required meetings, both virtual and in-person. If unable to attend a required meeting, a committee member must tender their resignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members urged to clear calendars, ensure technology access, seek supervisor permission/time off, secure funding and travel arrangements for LibLearnX, register for conference, and notify Chair of emergencies. Failure to meet attendance requirements may lead to dismissal and preclude future service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A committee member must resign immediately upon development of any circumstance that disqualifies them from committee service or that would affect or give the appearance of affecting their ability to carry out responsibilities fairly. Committee members will also be asked to resign if they cannot attend a required meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resignations must be sent to Chair, President, and Executive Director; Chair resignations to all members, PGC, President, Executive Director. Resigning Chair must forward current files to new Chair and Executive Director. President appoints replacement; if replacement not found in time, committee may operate one member down and adjust voting procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation — study terms, criteria, and related literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are urged to prepare by reading the committee manual (especially terms, criteria, definitions), books and articles about evaluation and criticism, practice writing critical viewpoints, and write critical analyses of past winners/honors structured around award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Appendix A Reading Lists and FAQs. Listening to book discussions (esp. with children) can be useful; active participation may be problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee participation duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must identify, obtain, read, and consider eligible books; meet suggestion/nomination deadlines; communicate with the Chair as needed; participate in electronic discussions as needed; and contribute to required meeting discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full participation is essential given workload; Chairs send letters of appreciation to employers/supervisors recognizing service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are responsible for identifying eligible books using publishers’ catalogs, review journals, publishing announcements, ALSC Notable lists, and attending Notables deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Notables Committee members or visit ALSC website; be proactive as publication pace increases throughout year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining eligible books — recommended sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members should obtain eligible books via publisher shipments, galleys at conferences (LibLearnX, Annual), review copies received at workplace, and browsing new titles in bookstores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are not to solicit publishers for copies (see Relationship to Publishers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining eligibility (publisher/author and publication year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members should refer to current terms, criteria, and definitions (including Appendix B) rather than precedent. Members should determine publisher locale, year of publication, and author/illustrator citizenship/residency (U.S. citizenship and/or residency is required; publisher must be located in the U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources include publishers’ catalogs, publisher/author websites, Library of Congress, Amazon. In ambiguous cases notify Chair who consults PGC; Chair informs committee of decision. For questioned release dates Chair may consult previous Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading eligible books — re-reading and workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are responsible for reading eligible books—potential contenders, suggested, and nominated titles. The reading load is heavy, and re-reading is often required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin early; maintain pace as publication increases; re-reading can reveal qualities not apparent on first read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note-taking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes need to speak to the award criteria. Keep complete bibliographic information, a short summary, and a critical statement noting strengths and weaknesses based on the award criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a convenient system (file cards, binder, electronic) but avoid public tools like Goodreads. Notes should be succinct, specific, include page numbers/quoted passages to justify points, and may include collected professional reviews (reviews should not be quoted during discussion). See Appendix C sample note-taking form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions process — monthly anonymous suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting early, the Chair solicits suggestions monthly via an online tool; suggestions are compiled in a table viewable by committee and remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No set limit on number of suggestions but members should avoid overloading the list. Suggestions help gauge support; members can re-recommend previously suggested books to indicate support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations process — three rounds and justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: In autumn the Chair requests three rounds of nominations: members nominate three, two, and two books (total seven distinct nominations) and provide bibliographic information and a justification statement (usually no more than 100 words) that speaks to the award criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may not repeat nominations on subsequent ballots but may nominate titles others nominated previously. Nominations are submitted via online tool, remain anonymous, and form the core list for LibLearnX discussion. Members must meet nomination deadlines on calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory meeting purpose (optional, virtual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional virtual meeting near start of year; Chair introduces members, may distribute calendar and invite PGC or experts; no official business; books are not discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open meeting; members urged to attend; useful for orientation and hearing evaluation techniques from experts or past chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Discussion Meeting (required, virtual) — practice discussion and agenda elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Held after Annual Conference; allows committee to prepare. Agenda includes reacquainting members, discussion of terms/criteria/definitions, review of procedures, responsibilities, role of PGC, a practice book discussion, and optional look at suggestions list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair prepares short practice list and may ask members to introduce titles. Practice discussion follows the same guidelines as final discussions but does not affect selection. Chair schedules meetings and appoints secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive book discussion limited to meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial book discussions among committee members will be limited to in-person or virtual committee meetings in order to promote inclusiveness and prevent cliques among members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email is explicitly not used for substantive discussion; use meeting time for substantive exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: LibLearnX Selection Meeting — preparation and list deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair establishes the list of books to be discussed at LibLearnX (all nominated titles remaining after preliminary deliberations, plus any late suggestions). The bulk of the list should be provided at least three weeks prior to LibLearnX; additions no later than one week prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair asks members to introduce selected books (typically those they nominated). Members expected to bring notes, copies of books, and biographical info. Chair communicates room/arrangement needs by October 1 to Awards Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection meeting book discussion etiquette and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: During book discussion: Use critical analysis; avoid plot summaries and generalities such as cute, nice, good, etc.; be clear, concise, refer back to criteria, speak to the group as a whole, be courteous and refrain from personal anecdotes; make comparisons only in relation to other eligible books; focus first on strengths before weaknesses; be even-handed; conclude with a closing statement from the introducer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not compare a book with an author’s body of work or with books published before the year under consideration. Provide page references/quotes in notes to justify points. See Thom Barthelmess and Vicky Smith articles for further discussion guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balloting procedure and point scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members list first, second, and third place votes in an online tool. The online tool assigns four points to each first-place vote, three points to each second-place vote, and two points to each third-place vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book must receive at least eight first-choice votes at four points each (total at least 32 points) and must have an eight-point lead over the next highest scoring book to win. If committee is operating an odd number of members down, Chair is recommended to refrain from voting. Awards Coordinator can adjust formula if committee is operating an even number down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-balloting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the first ballot does not produce a winner, the committee may not proceed to another ballot without a second round of book discussion. By consensus the committee may withdraw books with no or minimal votes from the discussion list; once withdrawn a book is permanently eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After re-opened discussion, proceed to second ballot with same point system; alternate between discussion and re-balloting until a winner is selected. Only one additional ballot is allowed for Honor Book selection (see Honor Books).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor Books — selection parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that Honor Books be named. There is no rule dictating the number of Honor Books to be named. There is an expectation that Honor Books be truly distinguished, not merely strong contenders for the Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee first considers whether to select Honor Books. Options: use winning selection ballot to look at titles with next highest points, or ballot one more time (only one additional ballot allowed) using titles from winning ballot that received points (winner eliminated). By consensus titles with no remaining support may be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary duties and minutes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A secretary is asked to take minutes on the order of business and procedural matters. No minutes are kept on book discussions or balloting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary prepares minutes after Initial Discussion Meeting and LibLearnX Selection Meeting; Chair reviews and forwards minutes and Quarterly Reports to appropriate leadership and Executive Director.
